prerequisites: Knowledge from the courses of Mathematics

learning_outcomes.text: The course intends to transfer the ability to correctly interpret the measurement results in the different areas of professional interest of the mechanical engineer. The fundamental theoretical concepts, the main criteria for analyzing the performance of measurement systems, the technical procedures for the correct use of the instrumentation will be provided.

At the end of the course, students will be able to choose the most appropriate components to configure a measurement chain for mechanical and thermal quantities in static and dynamic conditions and to analyze the main causes of measurement uncertainty. This knowledge is crucial for building decision-making skills based on real data, such as those of the main applications in the field on which the student will be called to work, being aware of the risks as a consequence of the level of confidence in the information available.
At the end of the course the student will develop critical analysis skills for choosing the most suitable tools for the intended use.
The study will allow him to acquire the correct terminology to communicate and discuss technical topics with colleagues, both in textual and graphic form.
The use of theoretical and practical exercises, as well as classroom discussions will allow you to speed up the learning skills thus stimulated by the practical applications of the proposed concepts.

syllabus_topics: BASIC CONCEPTS OF MEASUREMENT METHODS: general measurement system; experimental test plan

UNCERTAINTY ANALYSIS: measurement errors; Bias and precision errors; Fundamentals of Probability and Statistics; Uncertainty analysis: uncertainty propagation; multiple-measurement uncertainty analysis

STATIC AND DYNAMIC CHARACTERISTICS OF THE INSTRUMENTS: Calibration and Standards; first and second order measurement systems: Sensitivity; signal Amplitude and Frequency analysis in time and frequency domains
Data Sampling; Data Acquisition; A/D Converters
teaching_methods: Numerical practise with the aid of a projector and / or digital board, with direct intervention of the students during the practise
Laboratory practise with instrumentation brought to the classroom
assessment_rules: The final exam consists of a written test and an oral exam. The written test (30% weight) must demonstrate the ability to establish correct resolution procedures on the main theoretical and practical aspects of measurement. The oral exam (70% weight) requires the student to demonstrate acquired knowledge and the use of appropriate terminology by answering 3-4 questions related to the course topics, and sufficient command and language proficiency. A minimum grade of 18 is required for passing. For 30 cum laude, an excellent and comprehensive understanding of the subject, with autonomous and original critical thinking skills, is required, often with correct answers to additional challenging questions during the oral examination.
